title: Ransomware at 2 a.m.
oneLiner: Late on a Friday night, an attacker signs in to the VPN with a contractor's stolen password, steals an administrator password, and heads for the file servers to launch ransomware.
teaching: Ransomware gangs work nights and weekends because fewer people are watching. One on-call analyst works the queue slowly; automatic isolation kicks in only once encryption starts. An AI agent works at 2 a.m. as it does at 2 p.m., and only needs a person to approve.

labels.rootCause: A contractor's stolen password let the attacker in through the VPN, which doesn't require a second factor for contractors
labels.attackSummary: an attacker is inside the network and preparing ransomware
labels.hotEvidence: a VPN sign-in from a new country, followed by a password-stealing tool on the jump server
labels.ambiguousNote: A contractor signing in from abroad could be travel. The on-call analyst checks before waking anyone.
labels.objectiveImpact: Encryption has started on the file servers, and the backups are gone. Some company data is now locked.
labels.undetected: No alert fired at any point.
labels.mitre: T1078 valid accounts, T1003 credential dumping, T1021 remote services, T1490 inhibit system recovery, T1486 data encrypted for impact
labels.accessCut: the jump server was cut off and the contractor account disabled
labels.indicatorBlocked: the attacker's VPN address was blocked
labels.containDone: The contractor account is disabled, and the jump server and every server it reached are cut off from the network
labels.blockDone: the attacker's address is blocked at the VPN
labels.scopeNoneLost: No other system is still under the attacker's control.
labels.humanPivot: Pages the on-call engineer and pulls VPN and server logs, one console at a time.
labels.confirmAsk: Tier-2 tries to reach the contractor
labels.confirmReply: The contractor's manager confirms: "He's asleep at home, not abroad"
labels.playbook: SOAR disables the account and isolates the servers.
labels.rootMissingNote: Nobody checks how the attacker got in.
labels.fullFinding: The attacker came in through the VPN and hasn't reached the file servers yet.
labels.fullPackage: disable the contractor account; cut off the jump server; block the attacker's VPN address
labels.containPackage: disable the contractor account; cut off the jump server
labels.pivotText: The sign-in came from a country the contractor has never connected from.
labels.secondVictim: the attacker reached the file servers before anyone acted

events.title: Attacker signs in to the VPN with a contractor's stolen password
events.summary: Contractor accounts on this VPN only need a password. The attacker connects to a jump server used for maintenance.

events.title: Attacker runs a password-stealing tool on the jump server
events.summary: Grabs an administrator password left in memory.

events.title: Attacker signs in to 14 file servers with the stolen admin password
events.summary: Moves quietly from server to server.

events.title: Backups deleted
events.summary: The attacker deletes the backup snapshots so the company can't simply restore.

events.title: Encryption starts
events.summary: Thousands of files a minute are renamed and locked on the file servers.

rules.name: VPN sign-in from a new country for this account
rules.plain: the check for VPN sign-ins from an unusual place
rules.logic: An account signs in to the VPN from a country it has never used.
rules.triageNote: A contractor signing in from a new country, at night.
rules.agentTriageNote: A contractor account signing in from a new country at 1 a.m., to a server it rarely uses. Investigating.

rules.name: Password-stealing tool detected
rules.logic: A known credential-dumping technique on a server.
rules.triageNote: A password-stealing tool on the jump server. Someone is inside.
rules.agentTriageNote: Password theft on the same server the contractor just signed in to.

rules.name: Mass file renaming (ransomware behavior)
rules.plain: the check for ransomware-style mass file changes
rules.logic: Thousands of files renamed per minute on several servers.
rules.autoContainNote: The endpoint security tool sees thousands of files renamed per minute and isolates the servers on its own.
